text: Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites. There they camped before crossing over.

versions.text: Early in the morning Joshua rose, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites. There they camped before crossing over.
versions.explanation: The inverted "Early in the morning Joshua rose" is slightly stilted for oral reading; the natural subject-verb order flows better and matches the Hebrew narrative sequence.

text: At the end of three days the officers went through the camp
and gave the people this command: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, carried by the Levitical priests, break camp and follow it.
But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and it; do not come near it. This way you will know the road to take, since you have never traveled it before."
Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."
Then Joshua said to the priests, "Lift the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." So they lifted the ark of the covenant and went on before them.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.
Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's waters, stand still in the Jordan.'"
Then Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."

And Joshua said, "By this you will know that the living God is among you and that he will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is going to cross the Jordan ahead of you.
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.

And when the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off—the water flowing down from upstream—and they will stand in a single heap."

versions.text: And when the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the water flowing down from upstream will be cut off and stand in a single heap."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two clauses: "the waters of the Jordan will be cut off" followed by the appositional "the waters flowing down from above." The current rendering collapses them, losing the emphatic naming of the Jordan's waters that anchors the promise.

text: So the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of them.

Now the Jordan was overflowing all its banks, as it does all through the harvest season. But as soon as those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying it touched the water's edge,

versions.text: Now the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the harvest season. But as soon as those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying it touched the water's edge,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause describes the river's condition at that moment (a circumstantial clause), while the present-tense "overflows" reads as a general statement and clashes with the past-tense narrative that follows. A past-tense form with the habitual note keeps both senses and smooths the read-aloud rhythm.

text: the water flowing down from upstream stopped and stood in a single heap a great distance away, at Adam, the town near Zarethan, while the water flowing down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
